claims.text: In-situ high-temperature transmission electron microscopy can elucidate oxidation mechanisms and nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The initial material is an as-additively manufactured, dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
The proposed intervention is in-situ HT-TEM under controlled atmosphere and temperature.
The proposed oxidizing atmosphere is dry air or oxygen.
Nanoprecipitates and grain boundaries are structural mediators of oxidation behavior.
Oxidation induces elemental redistribution and segregation at nanoprecipitates and grain boundaries.
The oxidation-induced redistribution and segregation lead to formation of a protective oxide scale.
The additively manufactured alloy will exhibit a 20–30% lower oxidation rate than its as-cast and wrought counterparts.
Oxidation rate will be assessed through weight gain per unit area.
The comparison baseline consists of as-cast and wrought Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Impurities, defects, and sample preparation may influence oxidation behavior and measurement accuracy.
Failure to achieve at least a 15% oxidation-rate reduction relative to the as-cast and wrought counterparts falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted reduction is 20–30%, but the falsification threshold is below 15%; therefore, an observed reduction of 15–19% would fail to meet the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

Weight gain per unit area is specified as an in-situ HT-TEM measurement, although the design does not identify a compatible gravimetric method or a separate oxidation test for obtaining this bulk quantity.
